findings.title: BCB Resolution 588: Self-Custody Wallet Reporting to COAF Begins 1 October 2026 — 3 Days
findings.summary: BCB Resolution 588 (24 September 2026) requires BCB-authorised exchanges to report all transfers to or from a self-custody wallet of USD 10,000 or more to COAF effective 1 October 2026. This is a surveillance obligation, not a ban on self-custody. Resolution 589 separately prohibits dealings with BCB-unauthorised VASPs from 6 November 2026 (WATCH below).
findings.client_impact: Brazilian-resident clients or FGC clients using Brazilian exchanges to transfer crypto to personal wallets will have those transactions automatically reported to Brazil's AML authority (COAF) starting 1 October. Advisers should confirm client exchanges are BCB-authorised and that clients with significant self-custody activity are aware their on-chain transfers will be visible to COAF from this week.
findings.urgency_reason: Three-day deadline (1 October 2026). Clients must be notified today; their exchanges must be confirmed as BCB-authorised before the reporting regime starts. Failure to engage now means clients are caught unprepared at go-live.

findings.title: Panama Decree 25/2026: Controlling Person Threshold Cut to 10% — FATCA/CRS Review Overdue
findings.summary: Executive Decree 25 of 2026 (signed 29 June 2026) reduced the FATCA/CRS Controlling Person ownership threshold from 25% to 10% for Panama entities, aligning with FATF recommendations. Trust settlors and foundation founders remain Controlling Persons regardless of percentage. KPMG flagged the change in August 2026; STEP has confirmed it materially expands information exchange scope for Panama structures.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients holding 10–24% in Panama companies, foundations, or trusts must now be identified and reported as Controlling Persons for FATCA/CRS purposes — a population previously excluded. FGC should immediately audit beneficial ownership registers for all Panama-domiciled structures, identify newly captured individuals, and update self-certifications before the next reporting cycle.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in effect since 29 June 2026. Clients with Panama structures may have already missed the first reporting cycle that captures the new 10% threshold; delayed review increases exposure to non-compliance penalties across FATCA partner countries and CRS participating jurisdictions.

findings.title: Cayman DITC CRS Compliance Form Deadline Passed 15 September — Delinquent Filers Must Act Now
findings.summary: The Cayman DITC CRS Compliance Form for 2025 reporting year data was due 15 September 2026 (13 days ago). The FATCA/CRS XML submission deadline was 31 July 2026. From the 2027 cycle onwards, both deadlines shift to 30 June. CRS XML Schema 3.0 is required for all 2025-year submissions.
findings.client_impact: Any Cayman-registered financial institution (fund, holding company, trustee) that has not filed its CRS Compliance Form or submitted its FATCA/CRS XML data for 2025 is currently delinquent with the DITC and should file immediately to mitigate penalties. All entities must also note the permanent deadline change: future CRS filings due 30 June each year from the 2027 cycle onwards.
findings.urgency_reason: The 15 September 2026 deadline has passed; delinquent filers are in breach of Cayman DITC obligations. Immediate remediation filing is required for any entity that has not yet submitted.

findings.title: BCB Resolution 589: Dealings with Unauthorised VASPs Prohibited from 6 November 2026
findings.summary: BCB Resolution 589 prohibits BCB-authorised Brazilian exchanges from dealing with BCB-unauthorised VASPs from 6 November 2026 (extended from the original 1 October deadline). New supervisory data requirements on customer balances, proof of reserves, custody positions, and staked assets take effect 1 January 2027.
findings.client_impact: Clients whose crypto assets are held with or routed through foreign exchanges not authorised by the BCB must migrate to authorised custodians before 6 November 2026; failure to do so will prevent Brazilian exchanges from settling cross-border crypto transactions on their behalf from that date.
findings.urgency_reason: 39 days to the 6 November deadline. Asset migration from unauthorised VASPs may require lead time; preparation should begin immediately even though the deadline falls outside the 30-day urgent window.

findings.title: SEC Risk Alert: Widespread Deficiencies Found in RIA Annual Compliance Reviews
findings.summary: The SEC Division of Examinations issued a Risk Alert on 14 September 2026 documenting systemic deficiencies in annual compliance reviews under Rule 206(4)-7, including policies lacking testing methodology documentation, reviews deviating from written procedures, and evaluations of superseded policies. This signals the SEC's 2026 exam priority: effectiveness, not mere existence, of RIA Compliance Programs.
findings.client_impact: FGC and its RIA clients should treat the Alert as a pre-examination checklist: verify that compliance policies specify testing methodology, confirm the most recent annual review was conducted per current written procedures, and update any policies that reflect superseded practices before the next SEC examination.
findings.urgency_reason: No specific deadline, but the Alert signals active 2026 exam priorities. Proactive remediation now reduces examination exposure during the current SEC exam cycle.

findings.title: SEC Launches Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit — Heightened Enforcement for RIAs and Fund Managers
findings.summary: The SEC established a dedicated Financial Reporting and Accounting Unit within its Division of Enforcement in September 2026, focused on accounting fraud, earnings manipulation, and auditing misconduct. The unit concentrates existing investigative expertise and signals elevated enforcement attention on valuation and reporting practices for RIAs, fund managers, and SPV structures.
findings.client_impact: Fund managers and RIA clients should review valuation methodologies and financial reporting practices for portfolio companies and SPVs, ensuring documentation, consistency, and independence; the new unit is likely to scrutinise Level 3 asset valuations and related-party disclosures as early targets given their inherent subjectivity.
findings.urgency_reason: Operational now with no specific filing deadline. Fund managers with complex or illiquid asset valuation practices should review documentation before the 2026 financial reporting season closes.

findings.title: DFSA CP173 Consultation Closed — DIFC Funds Regime Overhaul Final Rules Expected Q4 2026/Q1 2027
findings.summary: DFSA Consultation Paper 173 proposed the most comprehensive overhaul of the DIFC collective investment funds framework since 2010, including risk-based fund classification, an Employee Co-Investment vehicle framework, removal of the External Fund Manager regime, and enhanced hybrid fund flexibility. The 62-day consultation closed 7 September 2026; the DFSA indicated a three-month implementation period after finalisation. No final rules have been published as of 28 September 2026.
findings.client_impact: Clients with DIFC-domiciled funds should review the proposed classification framework with their DFSA-licensed fund administrator now, as the removal of the External Fund Manager pathway and new activity-based classification may require structural changes before the finalised rules take effect with a potentially short implementation window.
findings.urgency_reason: Final rules expected Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Monitoring the DFSA website for the policy statement now allows preparation before the implementation window opens.

findings.title: US Federal Estate and Gift Tax Exemption Permanently $15M Per Person — Existing Estate Plans Need Review
findings.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently raised the federal estate and gift tax exemption to $15 million per person ($30 million per married couple), effective 1 January 2026, with annual inflation adjustments from 2027. The GST exemption also increased to $15 million. The TCJA-era scheduled 2026 sunset was eliminated. The annual gift exclusion remains $19,000 per donee for 2026.
findings.client_impact: UHNW clients whose estate plans were designed around the scheduled TCJA sunset should have their documents revisited: strategies predicated on urgency of gifting before a lower exemption are now obsolete, while new opportunities exist for larger lifetime transfers without gift tax. State estate taxes (e.g., New York at $7.35M threshold) and offshore inheritance tax remain live issues requiring separate planning.
findings.urgency_reason: In effect since 1 January 2026. Any estate plan not reviewed since the bill's enactment (4 July 2025) may rest on outdated assumptions about exemption levels and sunset risk; no new deadline, but continued delay foregoes planning opportunities at the new higher baseline.

findings.title: Cayman CRS 2.0: Digital Assets In Scope from 1 January 2026; Principal Point of Contact Due 31 January 2027
findings.summary: The CRS 2.0 update effective 1 January 2026 extends the Cayman CRS reporting regime to digital assets including payment tokens, utility tokens, certain NFTs, security tokens, and electronic money products. Financial institutions must appoint a Principal Point of Contact with physical presence in the Cayman Islands by 31 January 2027. The Economic Substance Act (2026 Revision) published without substantive changes to the existing regime.
findings.client_impact: Cayman entities holding or managing digital assets face new CRS reporting obligations starting with 2026 data; wealth managers should assess whether client digital asset holdings or crypto custodians create new reportable accounts. All Cayman financial institutions must also confirm appointment of a qualifying Principal Point of Contact with physical Cayman presence by 31 January 2027.
findings.urgency_reason: 31 January 2027 Principal Point of Contact deadline is four months away; digital asset CRS data is being collected now for the first reporting exchange cycle. Both items require advance planning and administrative action.

findings.title: MAS Proposes Stablecoin Regulatory Framework — Public Feedback Deadline 16 October 2026
findings.summary: MAS published a consultation paper on 1 September 2026 proposing amendments to the Payment Services Act to introduce a stablecoin licensing regime for Singapore-incorporated issuers of single-currency stablecoins pegged to SGD or G10 currencies, and a recognition regime for qualifying foreign issuers. MAS would gain powers to designate systemically significant stablecoins for enhanced oversight. Feedback closes 16 October 2026.
findings.client_impact: Family offices and wealth structures using Singapore entities for stablecoin treasury management or cross-border settlement should review the proposed framework; licensing or recognition requirements could affect the permissibility or operational structure of current arrangements, and advance structuring decisions are preferable to reactive changes after enactment.
findings.urgency_reason: Active consultation closes in 18 days (16 October 2026). Clients with Singapore stablecoin activity should engage or at minimum track the outcome; final rules will follow within months of the close.

findings.title: OECD GloBE Information Return Finalised — Pillar Two Filing Standardised for FY Beginning 31 December 2025
findings.summary: The OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework released the finalised GloBE Information Return (GIR) in September 2026, applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after 31 December 2025. Updated administrative guidance covers Explicitly Conditional Taxes excluded from Covered Taxes, QDMTT Safe Harbour application under different fiscal periods and local GAAP, and a full legislative peer review framework for domestic minimum top-up taxes.
findings.client_impact: MNE groups with entities in Luxembourg, Ireland, Singapore, the Netherlands, or other low-rate jurisdictions must use the finalised GIR format for Pillar Two top-up tax filings; in-house tax teams and advisers should update GIR compliance models to reflect the new QDMTT Safe Harbour eligibility guidance and Explicitly Conditional Tax treatment.
findings.urgency_reason: Applies to the current fiscal year (calendar-year MNEs). GIR filing systems must be updated to the finalised format before the first Pillar Two filing deadline in each compliant jurisdiction.

findings.title: CARF: 2026 Crypto Data Collection Live Across 48 Jurisdictions — First Exchange September 2027
findings.summary: The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework entered initial implementation across 48 jurisdictions from 1 January 2026, alongside CRS 2.0. Crypto-asset service providers must collect and report exchange transactions, transfers, and certain retail payments in crypto assets. First automatic exchange of CARF data (for 2026) is expected September 2027. Cayman DITC issued reporting guidance in late 2025; Cayman-based CASPs are live from 1 January 2026.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients transacting in crypto assets through any of the 48 CARF-participating jurisdictions should assume their 2026 activity will be automatically shared with their home tax authority in September 2027; undisclosed or under-reported crypto holdings in CARF-scope jurisdictions carry material disclosure risk that is best normalised before year-end 2026.
findings.urgency_reason: 2026 crypto data is being collected now. The September 2027 exchange window means year-end 2026 is the practical last point for clients to voluntarily disclose before automatic reporting reaches their home authority.

findings.title: SEC Registration Fee Rate Reduced 37% to $87/Million — Effective 1 October 2026
findings.summary: The SEC announced a 37% reduction in securities registration and filing fee rates from $138.10 to $87.00 per million dollars, effective 1 October 2026 for FY2027. Applies to Securities Act Section 6(b) registrations, share repurchases under Exchange Act Section 13(e), and proxy solicitations and tender offers under Section 14(g). This is the second consecutive annual decrease.
findings.client_impact: Clients planning capital raises, share repurchases, or M&A tender offer structures involving US-registered securities will benefit from a 37% reduction in SEC filing fees from 1 October; transaction cost models for any pending deals should be updated to reflect the new rate.
findings.urgency_reason: Fee reduction effective in 3 days; no client action required — purely beneficial. Relevant only for transaction cost modelling on pending US capital markets activity.

findings.title: Luxembourg Draft Bill 8676: Single Tax Class (Tarif U) Proposed from Tax Year 2028
findings.summary: Draft Bill 8676 (introduced 6 January 2026) proposes replacing Luxembourg's current three-class personal income tax system with a single unified tax class (Tarif U) from tax year 2028, aiming for greater equity and administrative simplicity. Currently in parliamentary review; significant amendments expected.
findings.client_impact: Luxembourg-resident family office professionals, management company employees receiving carried interest, and non-resident beneficiaries of Luxembourg structures may see material changes to effective tax rates from 2028; early modelling under the proposed Tarif U is advisable for clients with significant Luxembourg-source income or structures being designed today with a multi-year horizon.
findings.urgency_reason: 2028 effective date; bill is in early parliamentary review with amendments likely. No near-term client action needed, but structures being designed today with a 2+ year horizon should flag the proposal.
